full_judgment:
In this rule the points which fall for consideration by this Court are whether the Court of Appeal below rightly shifted the burden of proof on the plaintiffs in a suit for Specific Performance of Contract and whether the lower appellate Court rightly confirmed the finding of the trial Court regarding execution of a heba-bil-ewaz on the evidence on record. 

 2. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that although there is sufficient evidence on record to prove the execution of the heba-bil-ewaz executed on 9.1.78 by Abul Fazal the courts below merely on the evidence of PW 1, wife of the deceased executant Abul Fazal, held that the heba-bil-ewaz Ext 1 was antedated document without taking into consideration other evidence adduced by the plain-tiffs. She further contends that as soon as the plaintiffs have discharged their initial burden of proof regarding the signature of Abul Fazal it was shifted to the defendant to prove the contrary and in such a situation the courts below erroneously held that the plaintiffs failed to prove the execution of the heba-bil-ewaz by obtaining an opinion from Hand Writing expert. 

 3. The learned counsel has taken me through the judgments of both the courts below. A careful reading of the judgments indicates that the Court dismissed the suit for specific performance of contract instituted by the plaintiffs on the ground that they failed to obtain an opinion from Hand Writing Expert about the signature of the executant Abul Fazal to prove Ext. 1, heba-bil-ewaz executed by Abul Fazal on 10.1.1978. PW 1, wife of the deceased Abul Fazal, has in an unambiguous statement deposed that her husband signed the document. It seems that her statement has been corroborated by PWs 2 and 3. PW 2 stated that by his pen Abul Fazal signed the document in presence of the witnesses. PW 3 stated that Abul Fazal signed the document in his presence and in presence of the witnesses. In that view of the evidence adduced by the plaintiffs it is difficult for me to uphold the finding of the Courts below that the plaintiffs failed to discharge his onus in proving the execution of Ext. 1 by Abul Fazal only on the ground for want of opinion from Hand Writing Ex-pert. Where the initial onus is discharged by the plaintiffs by giving a slight evidence the burden shifts to the defendants to prove the contrary. In this case I am of the opinion that the plaintiffs were successful in discharging their initial onus of execution of the heba-bil-ewaz, Ext. 1 by Abul Fazal by examining his wife, PWs 2 and 3 and the signature of Abut Fazal being challenged by the defendants as not being genuine the onus shifted on them to prove so which they failed to discharge. In taking the view that the plaintiffs failed to discharge their duty in proving the genuineness of the execution of Ext. 1 by Abul Fazal. Moreover, the opinion of the Hand Writing Expert is not conclusive proof. The question as to proof of an agreement prior to heba-bil-ewaz in the instant case is immaterial in view of the pleadings. When the plaintiffs have successfully proved that the daughter gave the tazbi in question and that being consideration for execution of the heba-bil-ewaz there is nothing to prove further. It also appears from the evidence of PWs. that the daughter handed over the tazbi and the father Abul Fazal received the same. Apart from this it also appears from the evidence of PW 3 that Abul Fazal expressed his intention to make gift of the land in dispute in favour of his wife and daughter one year before his death. It also appears that Abul Fazal himself got the stamp paper purchased before his death. When it is proved that Abul Fazal before his death and the execution of the document purchased the stamp there cannot be any doubt as to the intention of making the heba-bil-ewaz. In that view of the matter I have no hesitation to hold that Abul Fazal had the intention to gift the property by way of heba-bil-ewaz in favour of his daughter and wife. Merely because two sheets of cartridge papers were purchased by the son-in-law of Abut Fazal it cannot be held that Abul lazal had no intention to make such gift as was held by the court below. It was not correct to hold that as Abul Fazal signed by a pen having different ink the execution of the document by Abul Fazal is not genuine. There is also nothing on record to show as it appears from the judgment of the court below that the signature appearing on Ext. 1 is not in the hand writing of Abul Fazal. In that view of the matter, I am constrained to hold that both the courts below committed an illegality in holding that the plaintiffs failed to prove the execution of Ext. 1 by Abul Fazal and dismissed the suit without considering the other evidence on record taking a wrong view regarding the onus. Accordingly, I set aside the judgment and decree of both the courts below and the suit is decreed.
